passages.text: “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job asks a question about the Almighty.
Job says, "Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment?"
Job asks, "Why do those who know God never see His days?"
passages.original: מַדּ֗וּעַ מִ֭שַּׁדַּי לֹא־ נִצְפְּנ֣וּ עִתִּ֑ים וְיֹדְעוֹ לֹא־ חָ֥זוּ יָמָֽיו׃

passages.text: Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.
passages.sermon:
Men act unjustly.
They move boundary stones.
They steal flocks.
They pasture these stolen flocks.
passages.original: גְּבֻל֥וֹת יַשִּׂ֑יגוּ עֵ֥דֶר גָּ֝זְל֗וּ וַיִּרְעֽוּ׃

passages.text: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
passages.sermon:
Evil men act unjustly.
They take the donkey from children who have no father.
They seize the ox from a widow as a pledge.
They harm orphans and widows.
They take away what little the helpless have.
passages.original: חֲמ֣וֹר יְתוֹמִ֣ים יִנְהָ֑גוּ יַ֝חְבְּל֗וּ שׁ֣וֹר אַלְמָנָֽה׃

passages.text: They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
passages.sermon:
Wicked men act with cruelty.
They push needy people off the road.
They force poor people to leave the path.
They make all the poor of the land hide.
The poor must hide together because of this oppression.
passages.original: יַטּ֣וּ אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים מִדָּ֑רֶךְ יַ֥חַד חֻ֝בְּא֗וּ עֲנִיֵּי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.
passages.sermon:
The poor are like wild donkeys in the desert.
They go out to work.
They search for food.
They look for something to eat.
The wasteland gives food to their children.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן פְּרָאִ֨ים׀ בַּֽמִּדְבָּ֗ר יָצְא֣וּ בְּ֭פָעֳלָם מְשַׁחֲרֵ֣י לַטָּ֑רֶף עֲרָבָ֥ה ל֥וֹ לֶ֝֗חֶם לַנְּעָרִֽים׃

passages.text: They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
Poor people work in the fields.
They gather food at night.
They collect what is left in the vineyards.
The vineyards belong to wicked people.
passages.original: בַּ֭שָּׂדֶה בְּלִיל֣וֹ יַקְצִירוּ וְכֶ֖רֶם רָשָׁ֣ע יְלַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.
passages.sermon:
The poor have no clothing.
They sleep at night without clothes.
They have nothing to cover themselves.
They cannot protect themselves from the cold.
passages.original: עָר֣וֹם יָ֭לִינוּ מִבְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת בַּקָּרָֽה׃

passages.text: Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.
passages.sermon:
Poor people suffer outside.
Rain from the mountains soaks them.
They have no shelter.
They cling to rocks to try to stay safe.
passages.original: מִזֶּ֣רֶם הָרִ֣ים יִרְטָ֑בוּ וּֽמִבְּלִ֥י מַ֝חְסֶ֗ה חִבְּקוּ־ צֽוּר׃

passages.text: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.
passages.sermon:
Evil people attack the helpless.
They steal from orphans.
They take babies away from their mothers.
They seize the children of poor people.
They do this to collect a debt.
passages.original: יִ֭גְזְלוּ מִשֹּׁ֣ד יָת֑וֹם וְֽעַל־ עָנִ֥י יַחְבֹּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
passages.sermon:
Poor people walk around without clothing.
They have no garments to cover themselves.
They carry bundles of harvested grain.
They remain hungry even as they work.
passages.original: עָר֣וֹם הִ֭לְּכוּ בְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וּ֝רְעֵבִ֗ים נָ֣שְׂאוּ עֹֽמֶר׃

passages.text: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.
passages.sermon:
Oppressors force the poor to work.
The poor crush olives inside the oppressors’ walls.
The poor tread the winepresses for others.
The poor do this hard work.
But the poor remain thirsty.
passages.original: בֵּין־ שׁוּרֹתָ֥ם יַצְהִ֑ירוּ יְקָבִ֥ים דָּ֝רְכ֗וּ וַיִּצְמָֽאוּ׃

passages.text: From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.
passages.sermon: In the city, people groan.\r\nWounded souls cry out.\r\nGod does not accuse anyone of wrongdoing.
passages.original: מֵ֘עִ֤יר מְתִ֨ים׀ יִנְאָ֗קוּ וְנֶֽפֶשׁ־ חֲלָלִ֥ים תְּשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וֶ֝אֱל֗וֹהַּ לֹא־ יָשִׂ֥ים תִּפְלָֽה׃

passages.text: Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.
passages.sermon: Some people rebel against the light.\r\nThey do not know the ways of the light.\r\nThey do not walk in its paths.
passages.original: הֵ֤מָּה׀ הָיוּ֮ בְּֽמֹרְדֵ֫י־ א֥וֹר לֹֽא־ הִכִּ֥ירוּ דְרָכָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יָ֝שְׁב֗וּ בִּנְתִיבֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.
passages.sermon:
A murderer rises when daylight is gone.
He kills the poor.
He kills the needy.
At night, he acts like a thief.
passages.original: לָא֡וֹר יָ֘ק֤וּם רוֹצֵ֗חַ יִֽקְטָל־ עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְי֑וֹן וּ֝בַלַּ֗יְלָה יְהִ֣י כַגַּנָּֽב׃

passages.text: The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.
passages.sermon:
The adulterer waits for the evening.
He watches for twilight.
He thinks, “No one will see me.”
He covers his face.
passages.original: וְעֵ֤ין נֹאֵ֨ף׀ שָׁ֤מְרָֽה נֶ֣שֶׁף לֵ֭אמֹר לֹא־ תְשׁוּרֵ֣נִי עָ֑יִן וְסֵ֖תֶר פָּנִ֣ים יָשִֽׂים׃

passages.text: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.
passages.sermon:
Evil people act in secret.
They dig through houses in the dark.
They break in when no one sees them.
During the day, they hide themselves away.
They do not come out into the light.
They do not know the light.
passages.original: חָתַ֥ר בַּחֹ֗שֶׁךְ בָּ֫תִּ֥ים יוֹמָ֥ם חִתְּמוּ־ לָ֗מוֹ לֹא־ יָ֥דְעוּ אֽוֹר׃

passages.text: For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!
passages.sermon:
The people in this passage are evildoers.
They love darkness.
For them, morning is like deep darkness.
They feel at home in the night.
They know the terrors of darkness well.
They are close to the fears that come in the dark.
Darkness is their companion.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יַחְדָּ֨ו׀ בֹּ֣קֶר לָ֣מוֹ צַלְמָ֑וֶת כִּֽי־ יַ֝כִּ֗יר בַּלְה֥וֹת צַלְמָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.
passages.sermon:
These people are evil.
They are like foam on the surface of the water.
They have no strength or substance.
Their share of land is cursed.
No one goes to their vineyards.
People avoid their fields.
passages.original: קַֽל־ ה֤וּא׀ עַל־ פְּנֵי־ מַ֗יִם תְּקֻלַּ֣ל חֶלְקָתָ֣ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ לֹֽא־ יִ֝פְנֶה דֶּ֣רֶךְ כְּרָמִֽים׃

passages.text: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.
passages.sermon:
Drought takes away water.
Heat takes away water.
Melting snow disappears because of drought and heat.
Sheol is the place of the dead.
Sheol takes away those who have sinned.
Sheol steals sinners just as drought and heat consume melting snow.
passages.original: צִיָּ֤ה גַם־ חֹ֗ם יִגְזְל֥וּ מֵֽימֵי־ שֶׁ֗לֶג שְׁא֣וֹל חָטָֽאוּ׃

passages.text: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is like a broken tree.
passages.sermon:
The womb forgets these people.
The worm eats them.
No one remembers them.
Injustice breaks like a tree that is shattered.
passages.original: יִשְׁכָּ֘חֵ֤הוּ רֶ֨חֶם׀ מְתָ֘ק֤וֹ רִמָּ֗ה ע֥וֹד לֹֽא־ יִזָּכֵ֑ר וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֖ר כָּעֵ֣ץ עַוְלָֽה׃

passages.text: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.
passages.sermon:
The wicked attack women who cannot have children.
They harm women who have no children.
They do not help widows.
They show no kindness to women whose husbands have died.
passages.original: רֹעֶ֣ה עֲ֭קָרָה לֹ֣א תֵלֵ֑ד וְ֝אַלְמָנָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְיֵטִֽיב׃

passages.text: Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful.
God uses His power to drag away the mighty.
The mighty rise up.
The mighty do not trust in life.
The mighty have no assurance of life.
passages.original: וּמָשַׁ֣ךְ אַבִּירִ֣ים בְּכֹח֑וֹ יָ֝ק֗וּם וְֽלֹא־ יַאֲמִ֥ין בַּֽחַיִּֽין׃

passages.text: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.
passages.sermon:
God gives the wicked a sense of security.
They feel safe and supported.
But God watches their actions.
His eyes are always on their ways.
passages.original: יִתֶּן־ ל֣וֹ לָ֭בֶטַח וְיִשָּׁעֵ֑ן וְ֝עֵינֵ֗יהוּ עַל־ דַּרְכֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
passages.sermon:
God lifts up the mighty for a short time.
They rise for only a moment.
Then they disappear.
God brings them down.
He gathers them up like everyone else.
He cuts them off like the heads of grain.
passages.original: ר֤וֹמּוּ מְּעַ֨ט׀ וְֽאֵינֶ֗נּוּ וְֽהֻמְּכ֗וּ כַּכֹּ֥ל יִקָּפְצ֑וּן וּכְרֹ֖אשׁ שִׁבֹּ֣לֶת יִמָּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”
passages.sermon:
Job speaks.
Job claims his words are true.
Job says, "If what I say is not true, someone must prove me wrong."
Job asks, "Who can show that I am lying?"
Job says, "Who can make my words worthless?"
passages.original: וְאִם־ לֹ֣א אֵ֭פוֹ מִ֣י יַכְזִיבֵ֑נִי וְיָשֵׂ֥ם לְ֝אַ֗ל מִלָּתִֽי׃ס
